questions: Should the target_value be compared as a string after converting all DataFrame values to strings, or should the comparison be type-sensitive (e.g., numeric 332 vs. string '332')?
If the DataFrame is empty, should the returned Series be empty (length 0) or have zero counts for each column (i.e., columns from the dictionary)?
Should the plot be a bar plot (as in reference) or any other kind (e.g., line, histogram)?
Is the target_value guaranteed to be a scalar, or could it be a list/tuple requiring element-wise matching?
Should the function handle missing values (NaN/None) in the dictionary of lists, and if so, how are they compared to target_value?
Are the dictionary keys (column names) always strings, or could they be other hashable types (e.g., integers)?
Should the plot be displayed (e.g., with plt.show()) or just the Axes object returned without displaying?
If the dictionary of lists has unequal list lengths across columns, should missing values be filled (e.g., with NaN) or should an error be raised?
